name: PT TBS Energi Utama Tbk

frontmatter.title: TBS Energi Utama — the marked parts, the market's discount and the dropped EV/EBITDA leg
frontmatter.summary: The bridge is fixed and coal is honestly marked at zero, but on the two company-specific legs - the marked parts and P/BV - the equity is worth about the price at the market's own discount. The EV/EBITDA cross-check that carried the ADD was struck on a konglo-inflated multiple and on group EBITDA including the zeroed coal segment, so it is dropped. HOLD, Rp423, 6.9%.
thesis: The ADD did not survive the EV/EBITDA correction. That leg used DSSA's konglo-inflated multiple on group EBITDA that includes the coal segment the SOTP marks at zero; without it the SOTP and P/BV blend value the equity at Rp423, a 6.9% return - a HOLD, not an ADD.

The corrected SOTP is about the price: after the non-controlling interest and the 44.0% market-implied discount, the marked parts are worth Rp396, against today's Rp396; the prior SELL double-counted the US$307.1m book elimination.

Coal is marked at zero from the segment P&L and waste is the value: US$41.4m of annualised waste-plus-EV adjusted EBITDA at the stock's own-history median, less the US$234.8m debt proxy, gives US$212.0m of equity - below the US$305.9m Cora enterprise price only because of that debt.
The P/BV cross-check at Rp263 is the honest counterweight: book is depressed by goodwill and the divestment loss, and the leg already carries a half-haircut to the optics-class receivable.

The HPS money is preference capital at the waste subsidiary, not value on day one: at an assumed high-single to low-double-digit coupon its annual claim is US$32.6m-US$49.0m, and it ranks ahead of the ordinary shares.

catalysts.event: RUPSLB to approve the HPS preference investment in SBTH
NTBE floating-solar project targeted for commercial operation

blocks.text: This revision moves TBS Energi Utama to **HOLD** with a twelve-month target of **Rp423**, a 6.9% return from the Rp396 price. The change is arithmetic, not a new view of the business: it removes the one valuation leg that did not belong. TBS remains a trust-controlled energy holding mid-transition from coal to waste, with the coal-fired plants sold and a BlackRock affiliate funding the waste platform; the question is what the ordinary shareholder owns after that financing [S9, S10, S12].

The Sector Lead's first finding is accepted, and the ADD does not survive it. The only leg above the price was the EV/EBITDA cross-check, struck at DSSA's multiple - a konglo name whose listed premium the konglo card excludes from a parent's fundamental value - on group LTM EBITDA that includes the coal segment the SOTP marks at zero. The engine reads group EBITDA, and no waste-specific non-konglo comparator is registered, so the leg cannot be rebuilt premium-free on a segment-consistent base. We drop it and the engine renormalises to 67% SOTP and 33% P/BV; the target is Rp423, a HOLD [S0, S11, S12, S24].

The second finding is closed. The breakeven marks are re-solved after the non-controlling interest on the two-method blend: parity needs a post-NCI waste mark of US$184.3m, the HOLD floor US$143.9m and the SELL boundary US$83.3m, replacing the pre-NCI figures that understated the fall. Terminal growth is zeroed. The nine-month print supports the operating story - revenue US$257.3m, an 18.0% gross margin, adjusted EBITDA at 17.0% and operating cash flow of US$20.3m [S22, S24, F121].

The discount is the market's own: the reverse DCF solves to 44.0%, above the card's band, and the base holds it with no dated catalyst. At the band top the target is Rp446, still an ADD; at the base it is Rp423. The P/BV leg and the preference coupon are the counterweights, and the driver bear corner at Rp240 is the path to a SELL [S0, data/base_rates.yaml, F157].

TBS Energi Utama is an Indonesian energy group that began as a thermal-coal miner, listed in 2012 and renamed from Toba Bara Sejahtra in 2022 to mark a shift toward sustainable infrastructure. It reports in US dollars and runs five segments: coal mining, coal trading, waste management, a residual power book after the coal plants were sold, and an "others" line with palm oil, renewables and electric vehicles [S8, S9].

The mix has inverted. In the first half of 2026 waste produced 61.2% of revenue and 91.8% of adjusted EBITDA; by the nine months waste and electric vehicles together were 66.0% of revenue and 71.0% of adjusted EBITDA, the share falling as coal and trading recovered [S12, S24]. Waste carries most of the acquired goodwill because it was built by acquisition [S12].

The waste platform, under SBTH Asia Holdings, operates three brands: Cora Environment, a Singapore municipal and commercial collector formerly Sembcorp Environment, with an energy-from-waste plant of about 360,000 tonnes a year; Asia Medical Enviro Services, with about 45.0% of the Singapore medical-waste market; and Arah Environmental in Indonesian medical, industrial and household waste across 15.0 provinces [S9, S10]. Together they collected about 760,000 tonnes in the first half of 2026, and the economics rest on collection density, permitted facilities and long municipal contracts [S15, S10].

Coal is smaller than the balance sheet suggests: about 7,087 hectares across three East Kalimantan mines run through ABN, IM and TMU, with reserves of about 14 Mt against planned production of 3-4 Mt a year [S9]. In the first half the mines produced 0.8 Mt and sold 0.6 Mt at an average price of US$55.2/ton against a FOB cash cost of US$38.2/ton and a stripping ratio of 3.2x [S12].

The other legs are real but sub-scale: a 6 MW mini-hydro plant, a 46 MWp floating-solar project that was 65.0 complete at the half-year, 13,883 Electrum electric two-wheelers and a 2,185 hectare plantation [S12, S9]. Highland holds 60.4% and PT Toba Sejahtra 8.0% through a Singapore trust, leaving a 31.7% residual; the controlling block sets strategy and how much cash reaches the parent [S9].

TBS straddles two industries with little in common. Thermal coal is a mature, price-taking export business; waste management is a recurring, contract-based service with local density advantages; waste is now the dominant earnings driver even though coal still supplies much of the collateral [S9, S12].

The coal arm is cyclical and small. TBS's realised price of US$55.2/ton sits below the headline HBA and ICI benchmarks because its grades are lower and its mix includes trading volumes, and the FOB cash cost of US$38.2/ton leaves a thin margin; the segment ran an operating loss in the first half [S12, S11]. With about 14.0 Mt of reserves against planned production of 3-4 Mt a year, the coal arm should be valued as a declining cash harvest, not on a stable multiple [S9].

Coal regulation matters three ways: the progressive royalty sets a floor under unit costs, the domestic market obligation requires a share of output at capped prices, and environmental licensing governs expansion and closure. Policy is pushing Indonesia away from coal generation while still relying on it for baseload, a long noisy transition rather than a clean exit [S9].

Waste is the opposite: a recurring service with high local density economics, long municipal contracts and permitted facilities hard to replicate. Singapore's collection is split into geographic sectors, Cora holds two, and its energy-from-waste plant turns non-recyclable waste into industrial steam; AMES's compliance moat gives it about 45.0% of the medical-waste market, while Arah serves a fragmenting Indonesian market [S10, S12, S9]. Competition is local and consolidating, with permits, density and disposal capacity as barriers rather than capital alone; the risk is that the acquisition-led roll-up pays rising multiples faster than it earns synergies, which is where the HPS capital will go [S10, S15]. Renewables are contracted but small, and the EV business lacks a proven durable margin [S12, S9].

External influences are macro and regulatory: dollar reporting, Singapore-dollar waste revenue and rupiah debt mean USD/SGD, USD/IDR and Indonesian rates all matter. The macro deck's USD/IDR path of 18,350 against spot 18,138 is context only, because the engine translates every method at spot [S0]. The look-through factors - coal, Indonesian rates, Singapore waste demand, USD/SGD and domestic EV and plantation demand - are recorded for sizing [S9, S10, S12].

Revenue fell from US$635.8m in FY2022 to US$365.9m in FY2025 as coal normalised and power moved toward divestment, and gross profit fell faster, from US$136.0m to US$29.7m [S0, S8]. FY2025 also carries a divestment loss of about US$96.9m and a net loss of US$161.9m [S17, S8].

The first half of 2026 shows the post-divestment business: revenue US$173.0m, gross profit more than doubled to US$28.2m, adjusted EBITDA US$25.7m and operating cash flow positive at US$14.6m [S12, S11]. The nine months extends it: revenue US$257.3m, gross profit US$45.2m at 18.0%, adjusted EBITDA up 39.0% at a 17.0% margin, the parent loss narrowing 72.0% to US$35.4m, operating cash flow US$20.3m and cash US$89.6m [S22, S24]. It is still an EBITDA improvement, not an earnings improvement: D&A and interest exceed operating profit [S20, S24].

Waste produced US$155.4m of FY2025 revenue and most of the first half, while coal mining and trading contributed about a third at a low margin [S3, S12]. We set FY2026E growth at -6.6% - the nine months plus a fourth quarter at the third-quarter run-rate gives US$341.6m - then 6.0% and 5.0% as waste annualises; no large acquisition is assumed [S22, S24, S12, S10].

We anchor FY2026E gross margin at the nine-month 18.0% and operating expenses at the first-half run-rate of 19.2% of revenue, because the data pack's SG&A is too low (FY2025 selling and G&A about US$72.0m, first half US$33.2m) [S8, S12]. The group is EBITDA-positive but EBIT-negative at the run-rate, the arithmetic of a capital-intensive transition [S12, S22].

The data pack's D&A was the G&A charge only. The audited notes show fixed-asset depreciation US$22.2m, mine-property amortisation US$31.3m, right-of-use depreciation US$11.8m and intangibles US$8.8m, a full charge of US$74.1m [S8]. The forecast uses the post-divestment run-rate, 17.6% of revenue, not the FY2025 ratio that includes divested-PLTU depreciation [S8, S12].

FY2025 operating cash flow was US$5.2m with capex of US$47.1m; the first half improved to US$14.6m against fixed-asset capex of US$10.2m [S8, S11]. We forecast capex at 10.0% of revenue falling to 8.0% and net borrowing of US$15.0m and US$10.0m [S13]. Net debt was US$307.3m at FY2025 and about 5.4x adjusted EBITDA at the half; the refinancing extends maturity but not leverage [S8, S12, S13].

Cash conversion deteriorated: operating cash flow over restated EBITDA was 1.41 in FY2024, 0.12 in FY2025 and 0.46 in the first nine months, and the negative accruals ratio is mechanical from the non-cash divestment loss [S8, S24]. Goodwill is US$85.5m, about half of parent equity, and the price is 2.22 times tangible book [S11]. The former Highland receivable of US$37.7m was assigned to CDG Trading at 6.8% and sits in US$43.2m of third-party receivables with CDG's ownership undisclosed; we classify it optics-class and apply the half-haircut (Rp263), showing the full write-off (Rp224) against reported book (Rp302) [S8, S11].

The holdco card calls for a sum of the parts with honest marks, less holdco net debt, less a discount treated as the base rate, not the opportunity [S0]. TBS fits it better than a consolidated multiple, which would price the mix and the consolidated leverage together [S0].

Cost of equity builds from a risk-free rate of 4.9%, an equity risk premium of 4.2% plus a country premium of 2.5%, and a beta of 0.9 levered to 2.3, giving a cost of equity of 20.3% and a WACC of 10.4% [S0]. The model's 7.5% cost of debt is close to the actual blended 8.2% and does not move the SOTP [S8, F160].

Each part is an equity value: coal after its own debt proxy, waste on an EV/EBITDA multiple after its debt proxy, trading, power and others at book [S11, S12]. The only deduction is the non-controlling interest of US$21.8m, against an ABN claim of US$29.1m; the full net figure is conservative because coal is marked at zero [S11 p.137]. The US$307.1m book elimination is the consolidation wedge, not third-party debt, and deducting it again was the prior FATAL [S11 p.150]. Coal is zero: at the realised price US$55.2/ton, cash cost US$38.2/ton, royalty, barging, selling/G&A and actual capex, the reserve DCF is negative after the US$120.4m debt proxy at both the run-rate and the plan volume [S8, S11, S12]. Waste uses the nine-month run-rate, not the first-half annualisation: 71.0% of adjusted EBITDA on a 17.0% margin and US$257.3m of revenue implies US$41.4m annualised, an EV of US$446.8m at the own-history median and equity of US$212.0m after the US$234.8m debt proxy [S22, S24, F145, F146]. The Cora purchase of US$305.9m is the market test; the equity mark is below it only because of that debt [S8]. Trading, power and others stay at book [S11].

The blend is 67% SOTP and 33% P/BV. P/BV at the 0.83 peer median gives Rp263, -33.7% below the SOTP; the gap is book quality - already net of the half-haircut (US$145.6m against reported US$167.2m), with US$85.5m of goodwill and the divestment loss [S0, S8, S11]. The EV/EBITDA leg is removed; P/E is unavailable on negative trailing earnings and no dividend is forecast, so the honest set is the primary plus one cross-check [S0].

The base holds the market's own 44.0% implied discount, above the card's band, because there is no dated narrowing catalyst: HPS is financing, not a distribution, and still needs RUPSLB approval [S0, S9, S15]. At the band top the target is Rp446, still an ADD [data/base_rates.yaml].

Holding coal at zero and the discount fixed, price parity needs a post-NCI waste mark of US$184.3m; the HOLD floor is US$143.9m and the SELL boundary US$83.3m [F113, F119, F120]. At the low end of the waste band the target is Rp269, a SELL; at the twelve-turn level Rp472, at the peer multiple Rp566 and at the Cora anchor Rp285 [F116, F117, F164, F165].

The discount-only bear is Rp366 and the bull Rp480 [S12, S15]. The driver corners are wider - Rp240 for a SELL when waste is at the low end, coal zero and the discount widens, and Rp678 for a BUY at the peer multiple with coal at its plan upper bound - and the probability-weighted driver target is Rp441 [F157-F159]. That weighted figure sits in the ADD band only because coal cannot go below zero; the most likely path is the base marks at a HOLD.

HPS commits up to S$555m of preference capital to SBTH in stages, subject to a shareholder vote; a fair-value preference adds cash and an equal prior claim, so it creates parent value only through what the cash earns [S10, S15]. The coupon is undisclosed; at an assumed high-single to low-double-digit rate the annual claim is US$32.6m-US$49.0m, most of adjusted EBITDA, so we treat it as debt-like mezzanine and add no headline value [S10, S12, F101, F102].

**Regulatory risk** is medium-likelihood and high-impact: the royalty schedule, domestic market obligation and environmental licensing can change the coal arm's unit economics, and the waste franchise depends on municipal contracts and permits in two jurisdictions [S9, S10]. **Commodity risk** is high-likelihood and medium-impact: TBS is a price-taker whose realised price is below the headline benchmarks, so a weaker ICI complex would compress the cash harvest before waste is large enough to offset it [S12, S9]. **Execution risk** is medium-likelihood and high-impact: the waste platform is acquisition-led, the HPS money is staged, and the solar project must reach commercial operation on schedule [S12, S10].

**Governance risk** is medium-likelihood and high-impact: Highland holds 60.4% and PT Toba Sejahtra 8.0% through a Singapore trust, and a preference claim ranks ahead of the ordinary at the waste subsidiary; the inbreng was completed without a fairness opinion because the entities are almost wholly owned [S9, S10, S16]. **Liquidity risk** is medium-likelihood and medium-impact: the residual outside the controlling holders is 31.7%, and the average daily traded value of IDR13.3bn is thin against a market capitalisation of IDR3,290.6bn [S0]. **Currency and rate risk** is medium-likelihood and medium-impact: dollar reporting, Singapore-dollar waste revenue and rupiah debt mean a stronger dollar or higher Indonesian rates compress translated value [S8, S13]. **Coal reserve risk** is the quiet one: a short reserve life turns the cash harvest into a run-off if reserves are not replaced [S9].

The scenarios mirror the same driver, the holdco discount, at probabilities of 25.0%, 50.0% and 25.0%; the values are Rp366, Rp423 and Rp480 [S12, S15]. The engine can shock only model inputs, so the operating distribution is given as computed facts: the waste band runs from Rp269 to Rp566, and the discount-shocked corners are Rp240 and Rp678 [F116, F164, F157, F158]. A SELL requires the waste multiple to compress to the low end while the discount widens, the mirrored operating downside, not the central path [S12, S0].

The signposts that would change our view are specific: a segment disclosure letting us mark waste on its own cash flows; a completed, priced acquisition showing the HPS money deployed accretively; a reserve upgrade or long-term offtake extending mine life; and a dated discount-narrowing event such as a buyback, tender or structural dividend increase from the waste subsidiary [S10, S15]. On the other side, a preference term sheet giving HPS conversion or upside participation at the expense of the ordinary would widen the discount, not narrow it [S10, S15].

Control is concentrated and the structure opaque at the top. Highland Strategic Holdings holds 60.4% and PT Toba Sejahtra 8.0%; Highland is owned by GLAS Trust, a Singapore trust acting for a passive private investment trust, and no single individual holds more than half [S9]. The annual report leaves 31.7% outside those holders; the data pack's free-float and insider fields overlap and sum above one hundred per cent, so we use the filing composition [S9]. Minorities have little influence over strategy, related-party terms or the pace of the transition [S9].

The auditor is KAP Purwantono, Sungkoro & Surja, an EY member, which issued an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 statements signed by the board on 9 March 2026 [S9]. That is baseline comfort, not a substitute for reading the notes - the D&A restatement comes from exactly those notes [S8].

Related-party dealings are small in the reported numbers but structurally important. At FY2024 the group carried a non-current receivable from Highland of US$37.7m under an acknowledgement extended to eighteen years and then assigned on 30 June 2025 to CDG Trading at 6.8%; the balance now sits in US$43.2m of non-current third-party receivables, and CDG's ownership and relationship to the controller are not disclosed [S8]. Interest income from Highland was US$0.7m in FY2025, so the receivable is not dead, but the assignment to an undisclosed third party is exactly the channel through which value can move between affiliates; we classify it optics-class and apply the haircut in the P/BV leg [S8].

On 16 October 2026 the group moved its SBT shares through SBTI, SBTH and SBTG at a stated S$138.2m, with new shares issued at an agreed subscription price and no fairness opinion because the entities are almost wholly owned [S16]. That is an intra-group subscription price, not an appraisal, so we treat it as a weak marker; the sequencing matters because the waste opco was moved under SBTH immediately before HPS takes preference shares there, directing the preference claim at the whole platform [S10, S16].

On pledges, the company's shares in operating subsidiaries and its accounts, receivables and inventories are collateral for the ADB, TLB and SEF facilities, while the controlling shareholder's TOBA shares are not disclosed as pledged; a subsidiary pledge is normal project finance, a controlling-block pledge would be a margin-call supply risk [S9]. The group paid US$17.5m of dividends in FY2025 including minorities despite a net loss, and the trailing DPS is Rp18.6; we assume the dividend is suspended on our negative near-term earnings [S8, S0]. ESG is central rather than incidental: the strategy is a decarbonisation transition, the PLTU divestments cut emissions by about 80.0%, and the waste platform is the environmental-services asset, while governance is the weak link that has to earn its discount rather than assume it away [S9, S10, S16].

Indonesian holding companies owned through family or trust structures have long traded at persistent discounts to the value of the assets they control, because minorities depend on cash actually upstreamed and control rarely changes hands. A transition story can narrow the discount for a while, but the discount is the base rate, not the opportunity.

The nearest dated catalysts are the shareholder meeting to approve the HPS preference investment and the floating-solar commercial operation date [S15, S12]. The HPS transaction is the more important: the preference terms, the staging schedule and the first acquisition will tell us whether the waste platform's capital is raised on terms that leave value for the ordinary shareholder [S10, S15]. The solar project is smaller but cleaner - contracted, substantially complete and additive to renewable revenue [S12].

The KPIs we monitor are waste revenue and adjusted EBITDA share, Cora's collected tonnage and plant availability, coal cash cost and stripping ratio, the reserve statement, net debt to adjusted EBITDA, the holdco discount to our SOTP, and the HPS deployment schedule [S12, S9, S10]. We also watch related-party disclosures and any change in the preference terms, the channels through which waste value reaches the parent's ordinary shareholders [S8, S16]. Until a dated event or a waste re-rate changes the arithmetic, the balance of evidence supports **HOLD** at the current price [S10, S15].

bear.narrative: The holdco discount widens ten points to 54%, beyond the top of its historical band: coal prices fall, the HPS money is deployed slowly and the preference coupon absorbs waste cash, so the market pays less for the parts. This table shocks the discount only - the SOTP marks are dated holdings values and the consolidated forecast does not re-price them - and the report states that limitation plainly; the operating downside is shown separately as a driver-based corner (waste 7x, coal zero, 54% discount), which is the SELL path.

bull.narrative: The holdco discount narrows ten points to 34%, back inside its 20-40% band, as waste EBITDA compounds on the HPS capital, coal cash cost stays low and the floating solar reaches COD on time. This table shocks the discount only, as the report states; the driver-based bull corner (waste 14.3x, coal +US$26m, 34% discount) is shown separately in section 4, not in this table.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 consolidated revenue was US$257.3m, 11% below the prior-year period, because the legacy coal business shrank faster than waste grew; this is a decisive change from the first half, which was flat year on year [S22, S24]. The nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the 2026 third-quarter run-rate of US$84.3m gives a FY2026E of about US$341.6m, which is -6.6% against the FY2025 continuing-operations base of US$365.9m, not the -12% used before: the old figure implied a fourth quarter of US$64.7m, below every quarter of 2026 [S22, S24, F1]. We then return to 6%/5%/4%/3% as the HPS-funded waste build annualises and the 46 MWp floating solar starts producing [S22, S15, S12].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the latest actual: nine-month 2026 gross profit was US$45.19m on US$257.3m of revenue, an 18% margin, more than double the prior-year period's 8% as the waste mix rose to 66% of revenue with electric vehicles and the coal legacy shrank [S22, S24]. The first half was 16.3%, so the third quarter stood above 20%. We anchor FY2026E at the nine-month 18% and hold it — there is no sourced reason for a margin fade, and a further uplift from waste mix is left to the bull case [S22, S24].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The data pack's 11.4% is wrong: the LK shows selling and G&A expenses of US$71.95m against US$380.2m of segment revenue in FY2025 (18.9% of the reported US$365.9m consolidated revenue), and 1H 2026 sales and G&A were US$33.172m on US$173.016m (19.2%) [S17, S12, F96]. We hold the 1H 2026 run-rate of 19.2% rather than the previous 19.5%, which had no source [S12].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The full FY2025 D&A charge is US$74.121m (F81: fixed assets 22.205 + mine amortisation 31.317 + right-of-use 11.790 + intangibles 8.809), 20.3% of FY2025 revenue, and the engine history now carries that full charge, not the pack's 15.7 or the fixed-asset 22.2 alone [S8]. For the forecast we use the post-divestment 1H 2026 run-rate: adjusted EBITDA 25.733 plus operating loss 4.770 implies a D&A plus PLN/other add-back of 30.503 on revenue 173.016 (17.6%, F98). The 20.3% FY2025 ratio includes divested-PLTU depreciation and higher mine amortisation and is not the forward run-rate [S12].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was US$47.1m (12.9% of revenue), including mine-property additions of US$37.2m and fixed assets of US$9.8m [S8]. The 46 MWp floating-solar project is 65% complete with COD targeted for Q4 2026, so capex stays elevated: 10% in FY2026E, 9% in FY2027E and 8% long run [S12].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was US$9.1m on US$365.9m of revenue (2.5%), and the group describes disciplined working-capital management [S8, S3]. We hold 3.0% of revenue, above the actual to allow for the waste business's receivable build.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025's effective rate is meaningless on a loss; FY2024 paid US$14.1m on US$36.9m of pre-tax profit (38.2%), above the 22% statutory rate because of non-deductible items [S8]. We use the 22% statutory rate on positive pre-tax profit.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance costs were US$26.0m on opening debt of US$341.9m (7.6%); the June 2026 DBS-led syndicated facility of up to S$385m refinances the older loans [S8, S13]. We use 7.5% on opening debt.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income was US$3.9m on opening cash of US$67.8m (5.8%); 1H 2026 interest income was US$2.8m [S8, S12]. We use 5.5% on opening cash.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The June 2026 DBS-led facility of up to S$385m is for refinancing, working capital and subsidiary capex, so it is not purely refinancing [S13]. We model US$15m of net draws in FY2026E and US$10m in FY2027E for working capital and subsidiary capex, then zero: the HPS preference is capital at SBTH and does not sit at the parent [S10, S13]. The quarter-end debt line was flat ($392.9m at FY2025 vs $393.0m at 1H 2026), which caps the near-term draw [S8, S12].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: the FY2025 loss on the PLTU divestment (US$96.9m) and the FX loss are non-recurring and excluded from the forecast [S8, S17].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities were 40.7% of FY2024 net profit and the minority balance sheet interest is US$21.8m (about 11% of equity) at 1H 2026 [S8, S11]. We use 25%, allowing for the HPS preference claim at the waste subsidiary to sit ahead of the ordinary minority [S10].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 cash dividends were US$17.5m against a net loss, so the payout is not meaningful on negative earnings; the FY2024 DPS of Rp21.98 was paid out of a US$28.5m parent profit [S8, S0]. We assume 30% of parent profit once earnings recover, consistent with the historical record.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares rose from 8,249.4m at FY2025 to 8,309.6m at 1H 2026 as the MSOP/ESOP issued shares without pre-emptive rights; we assume 0.5% a year [S8, S11, S9].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Zeroed per QC round-2 Q2. The holdco_sotp target is SOTP plus a P/BV cross-check; no DCF method runs, so terminal growth drives nothing and the old 2.0% was an unconnected input. The field stays at zero so the engine's input contract is met without implying a growth assumption the valuation does not use [S0].

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: The base now applies the discount the market is already paying, not the middle of the card's band. The reverse DCF at the 30 October 2026 price solves to an implied discount of about 44%, above the card's 20-40% range [S0]. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT §2 says the discount is the base rate, not the opportunity, and the house base rate for holdco-discount narrowing is only 0.33 over three years, so persistence or widening is the modal branch, not narrowing [data/base_rates.yaml]. There is no dated, completed narrowing catalyst: the HPS preference investment is a financing, not a cash distribution, and still needs RUPSLB approval [S15]. Highland Strategic Holdings holds 60.356% through a Singapore trust and PT Toba Sejahtra another 7.975% [S9], so the governance discount has not been earned away. Section 4 shows the 40% band top and the 54%/34% scenario range around this base. A dated buyback, tender, asset sale or structural dividend increase from the waste subsidiary would justify narrowing; none is sourced yet [S15].

challenges.challenge: The SOTP subtracts US$328.9m of "holdco net debt" from segment marks that are already equity values, and that number is the book reconciliation, not a third-party claim. The five book net assets sum to US$496.06m (F28-F29 284.29 + F30-F31 12.35 + F32-F33 77.79 + F34-F35 77.98 + F36-F37 43.65); 496.06 - 307.14 (segment-note elimination: 453.96 assets less 146.82 liabilities, S11 p.150) - 21.75 NCI = 167.17, which is exactly parent equity at 30 June 2026 (S11 p.8). The revision re-marks coal and waste to equity values (US$40.0m and US$253.4m, both already net of their own debt proxies) but keeps the same US$328.89m deduction. The segment-level finance costs already absorb the group's debt: 1H26 segment finance costs of US$16.60m in total and US$14.52m for coal+waste, annualised at the actual blended 8.2% (US$16.318m x2 / US$399.3m debt), imply ~US$405m of debt, essentially all of the US$399.3m group debt; the elimination column shows only US$0.28m of intercompany finance cost eliminated, so the US$307.1m elimination is not debt. The 7.5% proxy rate also overstates the segment debt: at the actual 8.2% blended rate the same coal+waste finance costs imply ~US$354m, not US$387m, another ~US$33m understatement of the marks. Deducting 328.89 from equity marks removes the subsidiaries' value twice. The corrected pre-discount NAV is ~US$405m (427.18 - 21.75) = ~Rp885/share; after the 30% discount ~US$284m = ~Rp620/share, and the blend target becomes ~Rp630, above the price. Even deducting a further US$50m of parent-only net debt the target is ~Rp576, still above price. The corrected SOTP (~Rp620) is almost identical to the report's own EV/EBITDA cross-check (Rp625, methods.ev_ebitda.value), which is the tell: the consolidated EV bridge is right there, but the same ~US$330m is deducted a second time from equity marks in the SOTP. The SELL is an artefact of this bridge.
challenges.answer: The bridge is rebuilt on option (b): the five marks are equity values, so the only deduction is the non-controlling interest of US$21.751m. The US$307.1m elimination is the book consolidation wedge (parent investment in subsidiaries and intercompany balances), not third-party debt; the 1H26 segment finance costs of US$16.60m against only US$0.28m in the elimination column absorb essentially all of the group's US$399.3m debt. At the actual 8.17% blended rate the debt proxies become waste US$234.8m and coal US$120.4m, replacing the old 7.5% figures. Corrected SOTP is US$495.1 per share and the re-run blend target is Rp542. This is below the red team's ~Rp630 because F2 (coal zero) and F3 (waste 9M base) are also accepted.

challenges.challenge: The coal reserve DCF's US$17.0/t "cash margin" (ASP US$55.2 less FOB cash cost US$38.2, F40-F41) is a gross spread before royalties, DMO, hauling, SG&A and other cash costs, and the DCF then deducts only US$2.0/t of capex and 22% tax, booking ~US$15/t of pre-tax free cash. The segment's own 1H26 P&L does not support that: coal-mining revenue was US$34.85m against segment cost of revenues of US$25.59m, and after selling/G&A and other costs the segment ran a US$3.87m operating loss (S11 p.150), i.e. the gap between the US$9.26m LK gross profit and the operating loss is US$13.1m of costs the DCF ignores. The company's two own gross-profit prints already disagree - S12 p.20 says US$4.3m (12.4%, ~US$7.2/t) while the LK's segment COGS implies US$9.26m (~US$15.4/t) - and the report reconciles neither. No royalty is modelled anywhere (params {} carries no licence; 1H26 royalty cash paid was US$3.34m, S11 cash flow), and the US$2.0/t sustaining capex (US$7.0m) is unsourced against FY2025 mine-property additions of US$37.2m (S8, ~US$10/t). Volume is the AR 3-4 Mt/yr profile (F46-F48) against 0.8 Mt produced and 0.6 Mt sold in 1H26 (F42-F43). Using the most generous company gross margin and the DCF's own capex/tax the plan-volume mark is ~US$+26m; on the S12 margin it is ~US$-44m. The +US$40m requires the full US$17/t gross spread with zero SG&A and zero royalty, and the report's own text concedes the DCF does not cover the debt at the actual rate.
challenges.answer: Coal is rebuilt from the segment P&L and marked at zero. The old US$17.0/t was a gross spread: 1H26 coal-mining revenue was US$34.851m, cost of revenues US$25.588m and the segment ran an operating loss of US$3.867m after royalty, barging and selling/G&A; the presentation's own gross profit is US$4.3m (12.4%, about US$6.8/t). At the actual costs and the actual 8.17% debt proxy the reserve DCF is negative at both the 1H run-rate and the 3-4 Mt/yr plan; the plan-volume upper bound is about US$+26m only if selling/G&A is ignored, and the presentation-margin case is about US$-44m. Zero is the limited-liability floor and the closest defensible base to that range. DMO is partly embedded in the realised price (1H26 domestic revenue US$8.287m of US$34.851m at about US$52/t versus about US$56/t export), so the separate DMO charge is not additive.

challenges.challenge: The update's central "what changed" is taken from three press summaries (S20/S22/S24) and never reconciled to the 1H segment note. 71% of a 17% adjusted-EBITDA margin on US$257.3m revenue (F132, F141) is ~US$31.1m of waste+EV EBITDA for nine months, ~US$41.4m annualised - 12% below the US$47.2m base used for the largest SOTP mark (F83 = 2 x US$23.6m). At 1H the waste segment was 91.8% of adjusted EBITDA (F39), so the disclosed mix share fell from 91.8% to 71%; with waste revenue flat in Q3 (157.3 9M less 105.9 1H = US$51.4m vs Q2 US$54.5m) that implies Q3 waste/EV EBITDA of only ~US$7m. Either the annualisation is too high or the press percentages are mutually inconsistent; the report calls the 9M picture "cleaner" without noticing.
challenges.answer: The waste base is re-marked on the 9M-implied run-rate: 71% x 17% x US$257.3m = US$31.06m for nine months and US$41.41m annualised, 12% below the 2 x US$23.6m first-half annualisation. The reconciliation is the Q3 mix: waste revenue was broadly flat in Q3 while coal and trading recovered, so the waste share of adjusted EBITDA fell from the first-half level even as group EBITDA rose. The waste mark falls from US$253.4m to US$212.0m; the EV mark is US$446.8m. The base multiple stays the sourced own-history median, and the 14.3x peer-median and Cora-consideration anchors are shown separately.

challenges.challenge: The report caps the waste sensitivity at 12x (F112), below the 14.30x peer EV/EBITDA median it uses on the group in the same section (model methods.ev_ebitda.multiple 14.2967; peers ADRO 7.47x, DSSA 14.30x, IMJS 19.89x). The waste platform is the only recurring, contracted business and 71% of 9M adjusted EBITDA; applying the report's own peer median to it gives 14.2967 x 47.2 - 255.9 = ~US$419m, gross parts ~US$593m, a SOTP of ~Rp403 and a blend target of ~Rp475 - above the current price - even before F1 is fixed. No waste-specific comp is used: 10.79x is the stock's own coal-era median (FY2022 6.34x, FY2023 40.97x, FY2024 10.79x).
challenges.answer: The sensitivity band is extended from 7-12x to 7-14.30x, and the 14.30x peer median is shown as the high anchor (equity US$357.2m, F147) with a blended target of Rp702 (F164). The base multiple remains 10.79x, the sourced own-history median, because no waste-specific listed comp is registered; the Cora purchase is shown as a market-tested anchor rather than a base. The report states the mix mismatch and the rating at the peer median.

challenges.challenge: The only market-tested price for the waste platform is ignored. The company paid US$273.2m net of cash for Sembcorp Environment/Cora in March 2025 (S8 p.18 "Acquisition of subsidiaries net of cash and cash equivalents acquired (273,249,466)"; S9 p.4 confirms March 2025). That is above both the report's US$253.4m waste equity mark and the US$101.6m inbreng marker the report anchors on. A base case that marks the platform below its own purchase price 18 months earlier, while waste revenue grew 41% and EBITDA rose, needs an explanation.
challenges.answer: The Cora acquisition is cited from the FY2025 LK: US$305.9m fair value of consideration for 100% of Cora (S$408.1m), US$43.9m provisional goodwill and US$262.1m of net identifiable assets, March 2025 (F150, F151). The current platform EV mark of US$446.8m is above that consideration; the equity mark of US$212.0m is below it only because the segment now carries US$234.8m of debt. Marking the whole platform at the Cora consideration less that debt gives US$71.1m of equity and a blended target of Rp386, a HOLD (F148, F165). The reconciliation is explicit in section 4.

challenges.challenge: The bear case (25%, tp 277) shocks only the holdco discount +10pp. It does not test the two drivers the report itself identifies as able to move value: the waste multiple (7x = F111 US$74.5m, ~Rp184 target, F116) and the coal mark (negative at actual volume, per the report's own §4 text). A bear combining waste 7x and coal zero gives a target far below Rp277. The scenario engine's driver set is inert and does not bracket the disclosed band.
challenges.answer: Mirrored driver scenarios are added as computed facts at 25/50/25: bear waste 7x, coal zero, 40% discount = Rp342 (REDUCE, F157); base 10.79x/zero/30% = Rp542; bull 14.3x, coal at its plan upper bound, 20% discount = Rp809 (F158); probability-weighted Rp558 (F159). The engine's scenario runner can only shock model inputs, and the SOTP holdings are not inputs, so the driver distribution is carried as facts and the discount-only limitation of the scenario table is stated plainly rather than hidden. The discount-only scenarios are still reported as the engine's official probability-weighted target.

challenges.challenge: Goodwill is US$85.5m at 1H26 (S11 p.6), 51% of parent equity of US$167.2m, and the P/BV cross-check applies 0.827x to that book with no tangible-book view (price/tangible book is ~2.2x). Cash conversion has deteriorated: CFO/EBITDA was 1.41x in FY2024 (119.1/84.5), 0.12x in FY2025 (5.2/43.2) and 0.46x in 9M26 (20.3/43.7), yet the waste is capitalised at 10.79x EBITDA. The negative Sloan ratio is a mechanical consequence of the US$96.9m non-cash divestment loss (F78), not evidence that cash conversion is healthy.
challenges.answer: Added the tangible-book view (goodwill US$85.5m, 51% of parent equity; tangible book US$81.6m; price/tangible book 2.22x; F149, F152, F153), the CFO-based check (CFO/EBITDA 1.41x FY2024, 0.12x FY2025, 0.46x 9M26; F155, F156, F169) and corrected the Sloan-ratio interpretation: the negative accruals ratio is mechanical from the US$96.9m non-cash divestment loss and is not evidence of healthy cash conversion. The waste mark is shown against that weak cash conversion.

challenges.challenge: The US$37.7m receivable from the controlling shareholder at FY2024 (F88; 4.22% of total assets, ~11% of FY2024 parent equity of US$357.4m) was extended to 18 years and assigned on 30 June 2025 to CDG Trading at 6.8% (F91); it then sits in US$43.2m of non-current third-party other receivables at FY2025 (F89), ~22% of FY2025 parent equity of US$194.1m and ~26% of the 1H26 parent equity, with CDG's ownership undisclosed. The 1H26 cash flow shows a further US$1.0m related-party receivable addition (S11 p.12). EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS §4 calls loans to affiliates the modal value-destruction channel on IDX. The report classifies it "optics-class, not manipulation-class" and the P/BV cross-check uses the full book with no haircut.
challenges.answer: The related-party receivable is quantified and classified. The US$43.2m non-current third-party balance is the assigned Highland/CDG receivable at 6.8%; zeroing it takes the P/BV cross-check from Rp302 to Rp224 and a half-haircut gives Rp263; the report shows all three (F167, F168). Per the house screen it is optics-class (disclosed and interest-bearing, but assigned to an undisclosed third party) and it warrants the haircut. It is not wired into the SOTP because the receivable sits at the parent/elimination level, which the segment marks already exclude; a second deduction there would repeat the F1 error.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue of US$321.96m (revenue_growth -12%) cannot be "the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter in line with the recent quarterly run-rate" as the assumption basis claims: 321.96 - 257.30 = US$64.66m for Q4, versus Q1 US$86.29m, Q2 US$86.73m and Q3 US$84.28m (F1, F22, F121); Q4 is 23% below Q3 and ~16% below Q4 2025 (~US$76.8m). A run-rate Q4 gives FY2026E ~US$341m (-6.6%) and ~US$57m EBITDA. The same false statement appears in §3 ("consistent with the recent quarterly run-rate").
challenges.answer: FY2026E revenue growth is corrected from -12% to -6.64%: 9M US$257.3m plus a Q4 at the Q3 run-rate of US$84.3m gives US$341.6m against the FY2025 continuing-operations base of US$365.9m. The old -12% implied a Q4 of US$64.7m, below every 2026 quarter. The assumption basis and the two report sentences are corrected.

challenges.challenge: The card's output contract requires a named+dated discount catalyst, the current discount vs the name's own 5y range, look-through earnings and leverage, and dividend-upstream coverage (sub payout x stake less holdco costs and debt service) - the last is called the card's "single most honest quality metric". The report has no upstream-coverage ratio and no look-through leverage table, even though the thesis is "what the ordinary shareholder owns after the transition is financed" and HPS ranks ahead at SBTH. It also does not compute the current discount vs the name's own history, relying on the card's 20-40% default without a 5y series.
challenges.answer: The card's output-contract items are added: dividend-upstream coverage of 1.22x on a consolidated proxy before the HPS coupon (F163), look-through segment leverage (waste debt proxy 5.67x annualised EBITDA, F172; coal debt against a loss-making segment), the current discount vs own history (trailing P/B 0.93x at/below the 0.966x own mean; the reverse DCF solves to a 44% implied discount), and the 30% base-rate rationale. There is no dated discount-narrowing catalyst, and the report says so; the base applies the card's central 30% base rate rather than assuming a narrowing.

challenges.challenge: §4 says "the stock's own five-year mean is [0.83]x book and FY2025A was the high observation; the current price is a premium to that history", but the model's own_history pbv mean is 0.966x and the current trailing P/B is 0.93x (model multiples FY2025A 0.928; FY2026E 1.10x). The current price is at/below the own-history mean, not a premium; the 1.882x "FY2025A" observation in the assumptions note is a historical-price figure, not the current multiple. The sentence substitutes the peer median for the own mean.
challenges.answer: Corrected. The current trailing P/B of 0.93x is at/below the own-history mean of 0.966x, not a premium; the peer median of 0.827x is a cross-check multiple, not the own mean. The report sentence and the assumptions note are fixed, and the current P/B is shown against the own-history range on the same trailing price basis.

challenges.challenge: The assumptions note says the peer EV/EBITDA median is 15.54x, while the model and packet use 14.30x (median of ADRO 7.47x, DSSA 14.30x, IMJS 19.89x). The peer set is three coal/conglomerate holdcos applied to a group that is 71% waste by 9M adjusted EBITDA and whose coal segment is a run-off; the mix mismatch is not disclosed. drivers_used is empty and no look-through factor tags are carried, though the report names the factors in §2.
challenges.answer: The assumptions note now says 14.30x (not 15.54x), matching the model and the peers (ADRO 7.47x, DSSA 14.30x, IMJS 19.89x), and the peer-set mix mismatch is disclosed in section 4. The look-through factor tags are recorded in assumptions.valuation.lookthrough_factors and in section 2; the engine's drivers_used stays empty because the holdco forecast lines do not reference a commodity or macro deck.

challenges.challenge: valuation.bridge carries +US$408.1m x0.8 and -US$408.1m x0.8, which nets to zero and changes neither the target nor the reader's information. The 0.8 is an unsourced guess at RUPSLB approval (S15 states only that the deal is conditional on it), and the commitment is "up to" S$555m and staged, so the full amount is an upper bound rather than an expected inflow.
challenges.answer: The two HPS bridge lines are removed; they netted to zero and added no information. The substance (preference ranks ahead; coupon quantified) is retained in the text and the valuation notes.

challenges.challenge: The engine's calibration gap (FY2026E EBITDA margin 16.4% vs FY2025A 11.8%, +4.6pp) is not addressed in qc_justifications - only weights.changed is justified and extreme_call is an orphan. The prose explains the mix shift in §3, but the record does not carry it, and minority_pct 25% (vs 40.7% FY2024 and a -US$0.7m FY2025 minority result) and capex 10% (vs 12.9% FY2025) are also below last actual without a source.
challenges.answer: qc_justifications now carry sourced entries for calibration.ebitda_margin (mix shift: nine-month 18% gross margin against FY2025A 8.1%, plus the post-divestment D&A ratio), minority_pct (1H26 minorities about 1% of the loss; balance-sheet NCI about 11% of equity; HPS ranks ahead) and capex_pct (1H26 run-rate about 6% of revenue against FY2025 12.9%, with the solar project still to finish). They appear as orphan_justifications because the engine raises a BLOCK only above its 5pp tolerance and these are inside it; no BLOCK is open.

challenges.challenge: Ownership percentages in §1/§6 cannot both be true: free float 28.95% and insiders 77.01% sum to 105.96% (datapack market.free_float_pct / insider_pct). The report also rates liquidity risk "low-likelihood" on an ADTV of Rp13.3bn (~US$0.7m) against a US$181m market cap and a 29% float, and says the shares "remain in the ordinary board" citing S0 (Yahoo data) rather than an IDX registry source.
challenges.answer: Ownership is reconciled to the annual-report composition: Highland 60.356% plus PT Toba Sejahtra 7.975%, leaving a 31.669% residual outside those holders (F154). The data pack's 28.95% free float and 77.01% insider fields overlap and are no longer used. Liquidity risk is raised to medium on the thin residual float and the average daily traded value against market capitalisation, and the unsourced "ordinary board" claim is removed; the report now states that the exchange registry is not a registered source in this system, so the board check is a filing check rather than an exchange-status confirmation.

challenges.challenge: The 10%-weight EV/EBITDA cross-check is the only leg above the price and it is decisive for the ADD. It is struck at 14.30x, which is exactly DSSA's multiple (ADRO 7.47x, DSSA 14.30x, IMJS 19.89x) - a konglo:true name whose listed premium VAL_KONGLO_REGIME §4 excludes from a parent's fundamental value, and whose premium BNBR's F2 removed from BNBR's own P/BV set in this same batch. The leg also capitalises group LTM EBITDA that includes the coal segment the SOTP marks at zero; §4 itself concedes "EV/EBITDA ... capitalises the coal-harvest EBITDA that the SOTP writes down", so the same base both marks coal at zero and pays 14.30x for its EBITDA. The company-specific legs do not support the rating on their own: SOTP Rp396.1 equals the price and P/BV is Rp262.8 (4.3% below price on the 60/30 blend of Rp351.6 before the house COE roll). With the EV/EBITDA leg removed and the other two renormalised, the today blend is Rp351.6 and the 12-month target is Rp423.2, a total return of +6.9% - HOLD, not ADD. At ADRO's 7.47x the target is about Rp420, +6.1% - also HOLD. The entire ADD margin therefore rests on the one leg the report calls the optimistic departure and on a multiple sourced from a konglo premium.
challenges.answer: The EV/EBITDA leg is dropped rather than rebuilt. Its 14.30x was DSSA's multiple, a konglo:true name whose listed premium the konglo card excludes from a parent's fundamental value, and the leg capitalised group LTM EBITDA including the coal segment the SOTP marks at zero. The engine's multiple method reads group LTM EBITDA and no waste-specific, non-konglo listed comparator is registered, so a premium-free, segment-consistent leg cannot be built inside the engine. Weights are now SOTP 0.6 and P/BV 0.3 with the leg at zero; the engine renormalises to 67/33. The re-run target is Rp423.2 (+6.9%), HOLD: the ADD does not survive, as the Sector Lead's arithmetic anticipated. The dropped leg no longer appears in the valuation table or prose.

challenges.challenge: QC round-2 FIX Q1 and Q2 remain open in the record. F113/F119/F120 and the waste_breakeven_note still solve parity at about US$122.2m/8.6x, the -10% floor at about US$77.4m/7.5x and the -25% boundary at about US$10.1m/5.9x without the US$21.751m non-controlling-interest deduction that the headline SOTP applies. Re-solved with NCI the thresholds are about US$144.0m/9.15x, US$99.1m/8.06x and US$31.8m/6.44x, so §4 and the note understate the waste fall needed for parity by ~US$22m; the note is not relabelled a pre-NCI strict-SOTP sensitivity. The 2.0% terminal_growth is also still set although holdco_sotp has no DCF method and the QC asked for it to be zeroed or annotated as not wired to the target. Neither item changes Rp456, but the record's own thresholds are wrong.
challenges.answer: The breakeven marks are re-solved after the US$21.751m non-controlling interest and on the reduced two-method blend (SOTP two-thirds, P/BV one-third): price parity now needs a post-NCI waste mark of about US$184.3m (about 10.1x), the HOLD floor about US$143.9m (about 9.15x) and the SELL boundary about US$83.3m (about 7.7x). The earlier figures were solved pre-NCI and understated the fall needed; they are replaced in F113/F119/F120 and in the waste_breakeven_note, which is now explicitly post-NCI. The unused terminal_growth input is zeroed, and the update is cut from about 9,500 words to 3,315, inside the 500-3,500 band.

missing_bull_case.note: The report caps the waste sensitivity at 12x (F112), below the 14.30x peer EV/EBITDA median it uses on the group in the same section, and never applies that median to the waste platform that is 71% of 9M adjusted EBITDA; at 14.30x the target is ~Rp475, above the price, even under the report's over-deducted bridge. The US$273.2m cash price paid for Cora in March 2025 (S8 p.18) is above the waste mark and is never cited.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear case (25%, tp 277) shocks only the holdco discount +10pp; it never tests the waste 7x mark (US$74.5m, ~Rp184 target) or a zero/negative coal mark that the report itself concedes at actual volume. Goodwill of US$85.5m (51% of parent equity), the US$43.2m former related-party receivable and the 0.12x FY2025 CFO/EBITDA are absent from the bear and from the P/BV cross-check.

assumption_realism.note: The two largest marks do not reconcile to the company's own P&L and disclosures: the coal DCF books US$17.0/t before SG&A/royalty/DMO while the coal segment lost US$3.87m at the operating line on US$34.85m of revenue, and the company's two own gross-profit disclosures (S12 p.20 US$4.3m vs the LK segment COGS implying US$9.26m) already disagree; the waste mark annualises a 1H number (US$47.2m) that the 9M 71%-share disclosure (F141) implies is ~US$41m. Credit: the gross-margin (18%) and SG&A (19.2%) anchors do come from the 9M/1H actuals, and the HPS coupon is openly labelled an assumption.

evidence_and_citations.note: Facts are mostly well sourced and derived ones are labelled COMPUTED, but the update's "what changed" rests on three press summaries (S20/S22/S24), not the unaudited 9M LK, and the 71% 9M share is never reconciled with the 91.8% 1H segment share. §4 calls the 0.83x peer median the stock's "own five-year mean" when the own mean is 0.966x, and free float 28.95% plus insiders 77.01% sums to 105.96%.

valuation_method_fit.note: The SOTP bridge is the book reconciliation (elimination 307.1 + NCI 21.8) applied to marked equity values, so it double-counts ~US$307m; the coal DCF omits royalty DMO and real capex; the waste is a blanket multiple off the group's coal-era history. The card's output contract items - dividend-upstream coverage, look-through leverage and the current discount vs the name's own 5y range - are not produced.

bias_and_tone.note: Credit: the report refuses to book the HPS headline and discloses the optimistic 22% coal tax. But the SELL rests on the double-counted bridge, and the prose overstates the book case: "the current price is a premium to that [own] history" is false at 0.93x trailing book vs a 0.966x own-history mean. Doubling the bear weight barely moves the target because the bear tests only the discount, not the marks.

signoff.notes: APPROVED (second sign-off; the prior RETURN is answered). HOLD, target Rp423, +6.9%. L1 verified on substance: the EV/EBITDA leg is dropped (weight 0), the engine renormalises to SOTP 67% / P/BV 33%, and the twelve-month target is Rp423.2 - the ADD does not survive without the konglo-inflated 14.30x leg. L2 verified on substance and arithmetic: F113/F119/F120 are re-solved post-NCI on the two-method blend - price parity needs a waste equity mark of US$184.3m (~10.1x), the -10% floor US$143.9m (9.15x) and the -25% boundary US$83.3m (7.7x); I reproduce 184.3 -> target 396.0 (TR 0%), 143.9 -> 356.4 (-10%) and 83.3 -> 297.0 (-25%). terminal_growth is zeroed, the report is 3,315 words (inside the 500-3,500 band), lint PASS, and QC round 2 PASS with the judge BLOCKs rebutted on the record (the SOTP deducts NCI only, not net debt 314.2; EBITDA = EBIT + full D&A reproduces the company definition). SOTP base verified: gross parts 345.79 less NCI 21.75 = 324.04m, x0.56 = Rp396.09 = price; blend 0.667 x 396.09 + 0.333 x 262.76 = Rp351.6, x COE 1.2034 = Rp423.2. BATCH: CONGLOMERATES is mixed (ABMM/ASII ADD, ADRO/BNBR/IMJS HOLD, DSSA/FOLK SELL), so there is no same-side tilt; BNBR's HOLD is konglo premium-kept on a fundamental 39% below its price, TOBA's HOLD is price-anchored through the market-implied discount - different mechanisms, no shared deck, no shared WACC/g/royalty input, and both discounts conservative (TOBA 44%, BNBR 38%). CONTAMINATION: none - no consensus, broker target or third-party estimate appears in the report, assumptions or facts; the peer multiples are house comps outputs. TWO POINTS FOR THE DIRECTOR, neither value-changing: (1) the SOTP leg equals the price by construction because the discount is reverse-solved at 44%, above the card's 20-40% band; the HOLD is therefore carried by the one-third P/BV cross-check (Rp263), and the card-band top would give Rp446/ADD - this is disclosed in section 4 and accepted as conservative, but the rating is not independent of the market price. (2) fund record's QC bias note (and my prior L1 line) say an ADRO 7.47x premium-free check "lands near Rp420"; I cannot reproduce it - 7.47x on the waste mark gives about Rp288 (-27%, REDUCE), and the report's own 7x band prints Rp269 (F116), so that line should not be relied on; the HOLD stands on the 10.79x own-history median and its 7x/14.3x bracketing, not on a peer-consistent multiple. Holdco opex remains uncapitalised (QC Q3 NOTE) pending a sourced parent-only figure, no value change in this version. Not published - the Director publishes.

bias.note: Round 2 re-audit after the Sector Lead's first return. L1 is resolved: the EV/EBITDA leg is dropped (weight 0), the engine renormalises to SOTP two-thirds and P/BV one-third, and the twelve-month target is Rp423.2 (+6.9%), a HOLD [S0]. L2 is resolved: F113/F119/F120 are re-solved post-NCI (US$184.3m/143.9m/83.3m; 10.1x/9.15x/7.7x), reconciling to within ~US$0.1m of the blend arithmetic, and terminal_growth is zeroed. The base is the SOTP at the 44.0% market-implied discount plus the 0.827x peer-median P/BV on half-haircut book; the marks are conservative but each sourced (coal zero, waste at the 10.79x own-history median, full US$21.751m NCI) [S11, S8]. Scenarios are mirrored on the discount (44% base, 54%/34% at +/-10pp, 25/50/25); the only one-sided driver is the coal floor, sourced to the negative segment P&L [S11 p.150, S12 p.20]. The HOLD is not a momentum artefact: the SOTP at the market discount equals the price, and the Sector Lead's own premium-free check (ADRO 7.47x) also lands near Rp420, so the rating survives L1 rather than depending on it. The one counterweight is that the driver-weighted target (Rp441, F159) sits marginally in the ADD band solely because coal cannot go below zero; the report discloses that rather than netting it. Net direction neutral.

findings.finding: The breakeven / HOLD / SELL waste-mark facts F113/F119/F120 are solved without the US$21.751m non-controlling-interest deduction that the headline SOTP uses. findings.finding: The holdco_sotp engine rolls equity[-1] + np_parent - dividends with zero dividends after FY2026E and PPE[-1] + capex - D&A charging the full D&A against PPE, so book equity turns negative from FY2034E and PP&E from FY2035E on a positive-FCFE base. The target is SOTP/PBV/EV-EBITDA and does not use the DCF or the 2% terminal_growth (holdco_sotp has no DCF method), so this is not a valuation defect - FCFE is positive every forecast year and net debt falls - but the unused terminal_growth should be zeroed and the mechanical book-equity rundown noted, or the template's PPE roll flagged to the Director as a tooling limitation. No value change.

The SOTP is a marked sum (coal at zero, waste on an EV/EBITDA multiple, the rest at book); P/BV uses the 0.827x peer median on a different metric. The EV/EBITDA leg is dropped per the Sector Lead's L1: its 14.30x was DSSA's konglo-inflated multiple and it capitalised group EBITDA including the coal segment the SOTP marks at zero, so it cannot be rebuilt premium-free on a segment-consistent EBITDA inside the engine.
